lore.statement: Zeus, Poseidon, and Hades are brothers, sons of Cronus and Rhea. They drew lots: Poseidon got the grey sea, Hades the murky underworld, Zeus the broad sky.
He is hailed as great god, mover of the earth and the sea, who holds Helicon and wide Aegae, and the gods gave him a twofold honour: tamer of horses and saviour of ships.
Poseidon came first to Attica and struck the acropolis, bringing up a sea. When the twelve gods gave the land to Athena, he flooded the Thriasian plain in anger.
The rivers Inachus, Cephisus, and Asterion judged the land between Poseidon and Hera, and gave it to Hera. Poseidon made their waters disappear.
Poseidon's wrath against Odysseus, who blinded the Cyclops Polyphemus, Poseidon's son, does not relent.
Hera, Poseidon, and Pallas Athena once wished to put Zeus in bonds.

variants.note: Apollodorus has Poseidon flood Attica when he loses it to Athena. Pausanias has him dry up the Argive rivers when he loses Argos to Hera. The profile keeps both as one temper: a lost contest is answered with water.
Apollodorus gives Poseidon a sea at the acropolis; Pausanias shows him with the wave. The profile leaves his gift to the sea.

inventions.statement: Poseidon's domain troubles are the game's own.
inventions.reason: A harbour surge that wrecks boats and nets, and a quake that damages walls and homes, are troubles the game draws on a season's odds and a floor, damaging a building. The sources attest his sea and his earth-shaking; no source tells these episodes.

inventions.statement: His earthquake is a damaging strike on structures.
inventions.reason: The world has no earthquake or flood action but strike; it is a game stand-in.

inventions.statement: His decrees of the sea are told in play as legends.
inventions.reason: Legend is the world's only public telling; it is a game mapping.

inventions.statement: The harbour and the fishers who revere him are placed by the game.
inventions.reason: The sources give him the sea and its ships but no town harbour. The fishing livelihood is an invention.

inventions.statement: The drive weights and the starting dispositions of Poseidon are authored tuning.
inventions.reason: The sources describe temperament in prose; the numbers are a design choice to be revised against play.

troubles.statement: A surge wrecks boats and nets: the fish landing is damaged. Autumn and winter.
A quake damages harbour walls or homes: a building is damaged. Spring and autumn.
